Is Baltimore a city or part of a county?

Baltimore is an independent city, separate from any county since 1851. Baltimore County almost surrounds it, and Anne Arundel County borders it to the south. The Census Bureau treats it as a county equivalent, which is why city agencies handle jobs a county would elsewhere, from tax collection to land records.

The city sits on the Patapsco River near where it empties into the Chesapeake Bay. It covers 92.05 square miles, of which 80.95 are land. The fall line between the Piedmont Plateau and the Atlantic Coastal Plain splits it into a lower city and an upper city, with a high point of about 480 feet near Pimlico.

What are Baltimore's main areas and neighborhoods?

The city is divided into nine regions that match police districts: North, Northeast, East, Southeast, South, Southwest, West, Northwest and Central. Downtown and the Inner Harbor are in Central.

  • South and Southeast: Federal Hill, Fells Point, Canton, Little Italy and Locust Point.
  • North: Roland Park, Hampden, Charles Village and Mount Washington.

Tens of thousands of rowhouses give the city its look. Rowhouses became the dominant house type early in the 19th century, and many have brick or formstone fronts. Formstone was patented in 1937 by Albert Knight.

How has Baltimore's population and economy changed?

Baltimore reached its peak population of 949,708 in the 1950 census and counted 585,708 in 2020. Heavy industry declined, and the city moved toward a service economy, with Inner Harbor redevelopment starting in the 1970s.

Johns Hopkins Hospital and Johns Hopkins University are the top employers. Other major companies named include Under Armour, T. Rowe Price, McCormick & Company and Royal Farms. Services provide about 31% of jobs.

The Port of Baltimore dates to 1706 and serves more than 50 ocean carriers. On March 26, 2024, the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapsed after a container ship struck it.

What is the climate in Baltimore, and what does it do to a house?

Baltimore has a humid subtropical climate. The July daily average is about 80.7 degrees, January averages 35.8 degrees, and annual precipitation at BWI airport is 45 inches, with about 19 inches of snow a season.

The record high is 108 degrees (July 22, 2011), and the record low is minus 7 degrees (January 22, 1984). That is a 115-degree spread between the record extremes, and a roof or heating system here sees all of it.

How do people get around Baltimore?

Light RailLink opened in April 1992 and runs from Hunt Valley through downtown to Glen Burnie and BWI Airport. Metro SubwayLink opened in November 1983 and connects downtown near Johns Hopkins Hospital with Owings Mills.

MARC's Brunswick, Camden and Penn lines link the city with Washington's Union Station, and Amtrak serves Penn Station. BWI Airport is about 10 miles south in Anne Arundel County. The Fort McHenry Tunnel carries I-95 and opened in 1985, and the Jones Falls Expressway (I-83) was the first interstate built in the city.

How is real property tax billed in Baltimore?

Baltimore mails real property tax bills every July 1. The city rate is $2.248 per $100 of assessed value, and the state rate of $0.112 per $100 is collected on the same bill.

  • Bills are due on receipt, with a one-half percent discount if paid by July 31.
  • Interest and penalties begin after October 1.
  • Late payments accrue 1 percent interest plus a 1 percent penalty per month.
  • Owner-occupied homes can pay in two equal parts, the second before January 1 with a small added fee.
  • A pending appeal does not excuse late payment, but a successful one brings a refund with interest.

The City applies a Homestead Tax Credit that caps yearly growth in taxable value for owner-occupied homes at 4%. State assessments set the values: in the January 1, 2026 reassessment, residential values in Baltimore City rose 13.4% over 2023, phased in over three years.

What is the Baltimore tax sale calendar?

Baltimore holds a tax sale every May, and a house can become eligible when a non-owner-occupied property owes $250 or an owner-occupied one owes $750.

WhenWhat happens
Early FebruaryFinal bill and legal notice mailed
MarchList of eligible properties published in two newspapers
First week of AprilSecond notice, covering amounts through April 30
April 30Last day to pay to avoid the sale
Third week of MayAnnual tax sale, normally
Six months after saleBuyer may sue to foreclose redemption on non-owner-occupied homes
Nine months after saleSame right for owner-occupied homes

The city says it cannot waive the fees and costs that state law sets for the bidder. A Tax Sale Deferral Program protects a property for one year without erasing the debt. If a homeowner falls behind, paying off the balance by April 30 is the cleanest way out, and a sale to a cash buyer who clears the lien at settlement is another.

How many vacant houses does Baltimore have?

As of January 28, 2022, Baltimore had 15,032 vacant houses, about 13,560 of them privately owned. That number was announced when the mayor ordered a 30-day review of how city agencies handle vacants, after a fire and collapse at a vacant house on South Stricker Street killed three firefighters.

The city's housing department files receivership cases against neglected vacants, and it was on track to file nearly 500 in that fiscal year. An owner of a vacant or inherited house can avoid that process by selling the property before a case is filed.

What does it cost to transfer a Baltimore house?

The city transfer tax is 1.5% of the consideration, and the state transfer tax is another 0.5%, for a total of 2%. The recordation tax is $5 for each $500 of consideration.

Transfers in Baltimore are processed in person at the Abel Wolman Municipal Building, Room 1B, 200 N. Holliday Street. Document processing is open to the public on Mondays and Wednesdays only. Each turn takes up to three documents, and each deed can cover up to three properties.

  • Bring a lien certificate, an original signed and notarized deed, an intake sheet, a settlement sheet copy and the contract of sale.
  • Pay open liens in full before signing in.
  • Use separate checks payable to the Director of Finance for city transfer tax, recordation tax and any yield tax.
  • Simplifile is available for e-recording.

What must a Baltimore seller disclose?

A seller of a house with four or fewer units must give the buyer a state disclosure or disclaimer statement on or before the contract is signed (Maryland Real Property Code 10-702). The disclaimer states that the property is being sold as-is, except for known latent defects.

Sales by lenders after foreclosure, sheriff and tax sales, and fiduciary transfers from estates and trusts are exempt. If a buyer is not given the form on time, the buyer can rescind within five days after receiving it.

Baltimore City Public Schools run the city's public schools, and about 100,000 college students attend the city's 10 accredited colleges and universities.

More questions about Baltimore, MD

What is the Baltimore City property tax rate?

The city rate is $2.248 per $100 of assessed value, plus a $0.112 state rate on the same bill. A $100,000 assessment produces $2,248 in city tax.

When are Baltimore property taxes due?

Bills are mailed July 1 and due on receipt. Interest and penalties start after October 1, and a one-half percent discount applies if you pay by July 31.

What is the Baltimore transfer tax?

The city transfer tax is 1.5% and the state transfer tax is 0.5%, a total of 2% of the consideration. Recordation tax is $5 per $500.

When does the Baltimore tax sale happen?

It is normally held in the third week of May. April 30 is the last day to pay taxes and avoid the sale.

How much unpaid tax makes a Baltimore house eligible for tax sale?

The city lists $250 or more for non-owner-occupied property and $750 or more for owner-occupied homes.

Where do I record a deed in Baltimore?

At the Abel Wolman Municipal Building, 200 N. Holliday Street, Room 1B, on Mondays and Wednesdays, or with e-recording through Simplifile. Bring the lien certificate and notarized original deed.

Can I sell a vacant Baltimore house as-is?

Yes. Maryland allows an as-is sale with a disclaimer statement. Any liens, tax debt or open code notices still have to be paid or settled at closing.

Where is Bowie, Maryland?

Bowie is a city in Prince George's County and its largest municipality. It is the fifth most populous city in Maryland and the third largest by area, at an elevation of about 154 feet.

Published area figures differ: Wikipedia lists 20.55 square miles in its infobox, 16 in the body text and cites a Census Bureau figure of 18.51. The 2020 census counted 58,329 residents, up from 50,269 in 2000, 54,727 in 2010 and 35,028 in 1970. The median age is 42.3, and the city has 20,991 households.

How did Bowie begin, and why does Levitt matter to sellers?

The city began as a railroad junction. In 1870 Ben Plumb sold lots where two lines met and called the settlement Huntington City. It was rechartered in 1880 as Bowie, named for Oden Bowie, a former governor and railroad president. Old Town Bowie is that original core.

The larger change came in 1957, when Levitt and Sons bought the Belair Estate and built the Belair community. Bowie annexed the Levitt land in 1959 and was re-incorporated as a city in 1963. Most residents today live in that Levitt-planned community built in the 1960s, and its street names follow alphabetical themes by section.

Because so many homes date to the same era, buyers can compare one house against its neighbors easily, and a seller should expect questions about what has been updated.

What historic places stand in Bowie?

Belair Mansion, built around 1745, is a Georgian house once owned by Governors Samuel Ogle and Benjamin Ogle, and it is on the National Register of Historic Places. The Belair Stud racing operation ran until 1957, and Belair Stable is now a museum.

Other listed sites include the Bowie Railroad Buildings, Sacred Heart Catholic Church and Melford. Owners near these sites should ask the city and county whether any historic-property rules apply before planning exterior work.

Who works in Bowie?

Schools, healthcare data and local government lead the list. These are 2018 figures from the city's annual financial report, as cited on Wikipedia, and employers may have changed since.

EmployerEmployees (2018)
Prince George's County Public Schools1,178
Inovalon605
City of Bowie446
Bowie Baysox260
P.G. County Public Safety Communications195

A 2007 estimate put median household income at $99,105. Per capita income ranks seventh in Prince George's County and 65th in Maryland. I-595 and US 50 link Bowie to both Washington and Annapolis.

What roads and transit serve Bowie?

I-595 and US 50, known here as the John Hanson Highway, run east to west through the city and connect Washington with Annapolis. US 301 and MD 3 run along the eastern edge toward Waldorf, La Plata and Baltimore.

  • MD 197, 214, 450 and 564 are the other state routes through town.
  • MARC's Penn Line serves the Bowie State station.
  • Bowie State University, north of the city, has operated since 1865.

Which schools and parks serve Bowie?

Public schools belong to Prince George's County Public Schools. Bowie High is the high school, and the middle schools are Benjamin Tasker and Samuel Ogle. Elementary schools include Heather Hills, Kenilworth, Northview, Pointer Ridge, Rockledge, Tulip Grove, Whitehall and Yorktown.

The city has about 2,000 acres of parkland and open space, including Allen Pond Park with its ice arena, plus Foxhill, Buckingham, Somerset, Whitemarsh and Jericho parks. It also has 72 ball fields, three community centers, the Bowie Town Center and the 800-seat Bowie Center for the Performing Arts. The Chesapeake Baysox, an Eastern League team, play at Prince George's Stadium.

Who governs Bowie, and which tax rates apply?

Bowie uses a council-manager form of government under its charter, with Michael Estève as mayor, according to Wikipedia. The city police department is the primary agency, backed by county police, park police and the Sheriff's Office.

A Bowie house is billed by both city and county. For fiscal 2026, the General Assembly's staff table lists $0.8760 per $100 for Bowie and $1.0000 for the county. The county says its rate is reduced for incorporated areas but the county page does not state the Bowie figure.

  • The state adds $0.1120 per $100.
  • M-NCPPC adds $0.2940 and the Washington Suburban Transit Commission $0.0260.
  • The county bill comes out in July, and full payment is due September 30.
  • A principal residence can pay half by September 30 and half by December 31.

For a sale, the settlement agent pays the bill out of proceeds, so what a seller needs is the payoff amount for the current year.

What if a Bowie house has unpaid taxes?

Real property taxes still unpaid by the second Monday in May are sold to the highest bidder at the county's annual tax sale. The county's Tax Facts guide gives the late charge as 1.67% per month, and there is no excuse for a missing bill.

Treasury Customer Service, 301-952-4030, is the number for a payoff. A seller who is behind may still close, provided the arrears are paid from the price.

Does Bowie license rental houses?

Yes, through the city rather than the county. The county's rental page says Bowie is among the municipalities it does not license, and it tells owners to look up the property on the state's real property search: if the Town column shows Bowie, apply with Bowie.

If a former rental has a license problem or an unpermitted conversion, the owner may want to resolve it before a sale. County code compliance enforces its rules through a Notice of Violation or a Civil Citation. Ask the city which office handles code complaints for a property inside Bowie.

What do transfer taxes look like on a Bowie sale?

The county's transfer tax is 1.4% and its recordation tax is $2.75 per $500 of consideration, per a 2026 General Assembly staff table. The state adds a 0.5% transfer tax.

Who pays which share is decided in the contract. Title companies print the full figures on the settlement statement.

What must a Bowie seller disclose?

A seller of one to four units gives the buyer a state disclosure or disclaimer statement on or before contract signing under Maryland Real Property Code 10-702. The disclaimer says the house is sold as-is except for latent defects the seller knows about. Estates and trusts, bank-owned foreclosures and tax sales are exempt.

What payment options does the county offer Bowie owners?

Owners pay Prince George's County online, by phone, by mail or in person. Online fees are $1.50 for an e-check, $3.95 for a Visa debit card and 2.45% for other cards, and the phone line is 855-516-1830 with added fees.

  • Mail to P.O. Box 37050, New York, NY 10087, with the bill stub.
  • Counter at 1301 McCormick Drive, Suite 1100, Largo, open 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. weekdays, with no cash accepted.
  • A 24-hour walk-up slot takes checks, money orders and cashier's checks.

A Front Foot Benefit charge for sewer or water pipes in the street (WSSC, 301-206-8032) or a solid waste charge may also appear on the bill.

More questions about Bowie, MD

What is the Bowie, MD property tax rate?

The fiscal 2026 city rate is $0.8760 per $100, according to a General Assembly staff table. The county rate is $1.0000, reduced in incorporated areas, and the state rate is $0.1120.

When are property taxes due in Bowie?

Full payment to Prince George's County is due September 30. Principal residences can pay half by September 30 and half by December 31.

Does the county or the city license my Bowie rental?

The city does. Prince George's County says Bowie is on the list of municipalities it does not license.

What happens if I do not pay Bowie property taxes?

Taxes unpaid by the second Monday in May go to the county's annual tax sale. The Tax Facts guide lists the late charge at 1.67% per month.

Which high school serves Bowie?

Bowie High School, run by Prince George's County Public Schools. Middle schools include Benjamin Tasker and Samuel Ogle.

How much is the transfer tax in Bowie?

The county transfer tax is 1.4% and the state adds 0.5%. Recordation is $2.75 per $500. Confirm the exact split with the settlement agent.

Is Bowie in a flood or hail zone?

We could not confirm a flood or hail rating for Bowie on official pages, so check FEMA maps and ask your insurer.

Where is Annapolis, Maryland, and how big is it?

Annapolis is the capital of Maryland and the county seat of Anne Arundel County, on the Chesapeake Bay at the mouth of the Severn River. It lies about 25 miles south of Baltimore and 30 miles east of Washington, D.C.

The city covers roughly 8.1 square miles, about 0.9 of them water, which makes it the smallest state capital by land area. The ground is flat Atlantic Coastal Plain, and the highest point is around 50 feet above sea level. The 2020 census counted 16,751 households and a median age of 37.0.

Annapolis is the only incorporated city in Anne Arundel County. Its government uses a weak-mayor system, with a mayor elected citywide and eight aldermen from single-member wards.

How did Annapolis grow into a historic capital?

Puritan settlers founded Providence on the Severn in 1649, the town took the name Annapolis in 1694 and was incorporated in 1708. George Washington resigned his commission here on December 23, 1783, and the Treaty of Paris was ratified in January 1784.

The Colonial Annapolis National Historic Landmark District surrounds City Dock. The Maryland State House, begun in 1772, is the oldest state house still in continuous legislative use. Other landmarks include the Old Treasury Building (1735) and the Hammond-Harwood House (1774).

For a seller, the historic district is a reason to ask the city planning office about review rules before promising a buyer any exterior renovation.

What does tidal flooding mean for an Annapolis house?

Flooding is the most distinctive risk for Annapolis owners. Sea level has risen about 15 inches over the past century, and Hurricane Isabel in 2003 pushed the storm surge to a record 7.58 feet.

  • Non-storm "sunny day" tidal flooding hit 18 days between May 2019 and April 2020, up from 12 days in 2018.
  • The 1995 to 2005 average was about 2 days a year.
  • The city recorded 120 flooding events in 2024.
  • Ground was broken on November 3, 2025 for an $87 million City Dock project with floodgates and raised land, designed to protect against flood levels through 2060.

A flood-damaged house can be hard to sell on the open market, because a buyer's inspector will note the damage. An as-is cash sale avoids the drying-out, repair and re-inspection cycle.

What other weather affects houses in Annapolis?

Annapolis has a humid subtropical climate, with hot, humid summers and cool winters, and about 44 inches of precipitation across roughly 116 days a year. Summer highs reach about 86 degrees, and the record high is 106 degrees.

An EF-2 tornado hit the western edge of the city on September 1, 2021, with estimated winds of 125 mph.

A tornado or a hurricane surge can leave a house with damage that insurance and repairs take months to settle, which is when some owners choose an as-is sale.

Which neighborhoods make up Annapolis?

Within the city limits, the commonly named areas are Church Circle and St. Anne's, Main Street and City Dock, State Circle and Maryland Avenue, West Annapolis, the West Street arts district, Eastport and Parole.

Parole takes its name from Camp Parole, where paroled Union soldiers were held during the Civil War. Nearby communities outside the city include Arnold, Crofton, Crownsville, Edgewater, Gambrills, Londontowne, Millersville and Odenton, and those sit in the county rather than the city, so city tax and city rules do not apply to them.

Who employs people in Annapolis?

State government, the U.S. Naval Academy and tourism carry the local economy. The Naval Academy, founded in 1845, has about 4,500 midshipmen and roughly 2,500 employees. The legislature, governor's office and appellate courts are all based in Annapolis.

Employer (2018, excluding state and local government)Employees
U.S. Naval AcademyAbout 2,500
ARC of the Central Chesapeake Region502
Annapolis Marriott Waterfront215
St. John's College204
Comtech Telecommunications200

Recreational boating has largely replaced the old seafood trade. St. John's College, a private liberal arts school, opened in 1789 and traces its roots to King William's School of 1696, and the Naval Academy museum in Preble Hall draws about 100,000 visitors a year.

How do people get around Annapolis?

No major highway runs inside the city limits. I-595, US 50 and US 301 pass just outside, I-97 links to Baltimore and MD 2 leads south. MD 70 and MD 665 are the main roads in.

Annapolis Transit operates eight bus routes. Passenger rail served the city from 1840 to 1968, and the tracks were removed in 1976. Schools are run by Anne Arundel County Public Schools, and Annapolis High School has been open since 1896.

How is Annapolis property tax billed?

Annapolis owners pay three rates on one bill, and payments go to Anne Arundel County. For the fiscal year running July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027, the Anne Arundel County finance page lists $0.738 per $100 for the city, $0.577 for the county and $0.112 for the state.

  • Principal residences can pay half by September 30 and the balance by December 31, with a 0.87% service charge on the second payment.
  • The Homestead Tax Credit caps yearly growth in taxable value for a primary home: 10% for the city and 2% for the county. Applications are due December 31 for a credit starting the next July 1.
  • The Homeowners' Property Tax Credit is income-based, and the page suggests households under $60,000 consider applying.
  • Finance Customer Service answers at 410-222-1144.

The state reappraises one-third of properties each year and phases in increases over three years. In the January 1, 2026 cycle, residential values in Anne Arundel County rose 16.0% over the 2023 level.

What are the transfer and recordation taxes in Anne Arundel County?

A 2026 General Assembly staff table lists Anne Arundel County's transfer tax at 1.0% to 1.5%, with a 0.5% surcharge on transactions of $1 million or more. Its recordation tax is $3.50 per $500.

The state also levies a 0.5% transfer tax. Who pays each tax is a matter of the contract. A title company will print the numbers on the settlement statement, and a seller should ask for a draft early.

What must an Annapolis seller disclose?

Anyone selling a one- to four-unit house must hand the buyer a state disclosure or disclaimer form on or before signing the contract (Maryland Real Property Code 10-702). The disclaimer states that the property is sold as-is, except for latent defects the seller actually knows about.

Fiduciary sales in estates and trusts, bank sales after foreclosure and tax sales are exempt. A buyer who gets the form late can rescind within five days of receiving it.

More questions about Annapolis, MD

Does Annapolis flood often?

Yes, in low areas. The city recorded 120 flooding events in 2024, and sunny-day tidal flooding reached 18 days in the year ending April 2020. A City Dock project broke ground in November 2025 to address it.

What is the Annapolis property tax rate?

The county finance page lists $0.738 per $100 for the city in fiscal 2027, plus $0.577 for the county and $0.112 for the state. Bills run July 1 to June 30.

When are Annapolis property taxes due?

Principal residences can pay half by September 30 and half by December 31, with a 0.87% service charge on the second half. Call 410-222-1144 for the current due date on a full-year bill.

Is there a homestead credit in Annapolis?

Yes. It limits taxable value growth on a primary home to 10% a year for city tax and 2% for county tax. Applications are due December 31 for the following July 1.

What is the Anne Arundel County transfer tax?

The 2026 staff table shows 1.0% to 1.5%, with a 0.5% surcharge at $1 million or more. A separate state transfer tax of 0.5% also applies.

Do I have to disclose problems when selling in Annapolis?

Maryland requires a disclosure or as-is disclaimer form for most one- to four-unit homes, delivered on or before signing the contract. Estate, foreclosure and tax sales are exempt.

Can I sell an Annapolis house with water damage?

Yes. You can disclose the damage and sell as-is. A cash buyer typically prices the repairs into the offer, which avoids a drying-out and re-inspection cycle.
